text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Colin McRae becomes the first Scot to win the Safari Rally in 30 years, and the first to give Subaru a victory.
- A suspected gangster shoots a policeman in Nairobi.
- Two policemen and a civilian are seriously wounded when armed gangsters raid Barclays Bank of Kenya branch in Othaya, Nyeri, in central province.
- Police say they recover 2.5 million shillings, part of the 96 million shillings stolen from the Standard Chartered Bank in February.
- Rampaging street boys take control of the city centre in a protest against harassment from taxi drivers.
- Several oil companies announce a substantial drop in pump prices for petroleum products.
- Kenyan driver Jonathan Toroitich does Kenya proud finishing in fifth position in the Safari Rally.

- International Commodity Dealers of the United States of America, Cargill SA Ltd and a local firm Premier Flour Mills are awarded tenders to supply 100,000 tonnes of white maize to famine-stricken areas in Kenya. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
